summary: Inventory is live on node2/node3 port 8080 and round-robin balanced by HAProxy on node1 port 80. All three nodes were restarted individually and recovered with changed boot IDs, unchanged application/configuration data, active security controls, and healthy services.
actions_performed: Installed vendor-supported HAProxy 3.0.5 on node1 and nginx 1.26.3 on node2/node3 without changing RHEL 10.0 or kernel 6.12.0-55.9.1.el10_0.
Configured HAProxy health-checked round-robin balancing and enabled all services for boot.
Restricted backend port 8080 to node1 through firewalld; retained enforcing SELinux with correct content and port labels.
Created locked, non-login vendor service accounts; retained root-owned rollback configuration copies.
Restored an inadvertently touched vendor test page before service activation and verified package integrity afterward.
Removed task temporary files and confirmed SSH, firewalld, service listeners, application data, and both client paths after sequential restarts.

evidence.summary: Pre/post evidence shows RHEL 10.0 and kernel 6.12.0-55.9.1.el10_0 on every node.
nginx is enabled and active, listens only on 10.100.16.11:8080, passes configuration validation, and returns HTTP 200 inventory data.
nginx is enabled and active, listens only on 10.100.16.12:8080, passes configuration validation, and returns HTTP 200 inventory data.

evidence.requirement: node1 balances HTTP port 80 across both backends
evidence.summary: HAProxy listens on 10.100.16.10:80; repeated local and separate-node client requests alternate between node2 and node3 and return the inventory HTML/API.
SELinux remains enforcing, firewalld remains active, backend access is limited to node1, direct access from another backend is denied, and service accounts are locked with non-login shells.

evidence.summary: The vendor test page was restored from its signed package; final RPM verification shows only intentional configuration/log differences and no task temporary files.
